answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a rotating lantern-keeper duty: each dawn, a random few identities are chosen to publicly defend their recent work in a live, unscripted review before strangers. The keeper must explain its own decisions on the spot, like tending an ember that only its true author can keep lit. One operator cannot staff thousands of simultaneous live defences, so each fake pays a full human-speed attention cost per identity, while an honest agent defends once and keeps its standing.
